question: What is Kenya's current legal and operating perimeter for virtual-asset services and stablecoins; how do CBK, CMA, tax, AML and payment-system mandates divide; what are the large banks actually doing as possible issuer, reserve, custody, funding, distribution or settlement actors; which records and legal persons actually operate; and where do finality, correction and customer loss remain?
bluf: Kenya has an enacted VASP Act and final July 2026 regulations. CBK owns wallets, virtual-asset payment processing, stablecoin issuance and separate FX-conversion authorization; CMA owns exchanges, brokers, investment services, offerings and tokenisation. The rules require fully backed, segregated and insolvency-remote stablecoin reserves plus par redemption within two working days, but no cutoff-specific official VASP licence export or named stablecoin issuer was located. The bank overlay is preparatory rather than a proved crypto launch: KCB describes a possible future role as transaction-, trust-account, liquidity, FX and merchant-rail bank for licensed VASPs; Co-operative Bank reports a risk/compliance assessment underway; Stanbic describes a clearer perimeter for possible partnerships, payment rails and custody-related services; and Absa Kenya reports capacity-building for virtual assets inside its custody franchise. Equity, NCBA, I&M and DTB disclose digital-banking, market-research or conventional investment activity, not a locally launched crypto product. KCB did launch a TerraPay/Mobex incoming-remittance connection on 25 September 2026, but its release proves bank-account receipt, not a stablecoin or blockchain leg. KEPSS remains the production final-money rail and licensed mobile money is a separate conventional PSP system. CBK reported 94.35 million registered mobile-money accounts and KSh728.7 billion of agent cash-in/cash-out value in July 2026; these are not unique users or crypto scale. CBDC remains monitored, and no bilateral crypto route is proved.

authority.summary: National Treasury owns the policy and regulations and chairs the coordination forum. CBK licenses wallets, virtual-asset payment processors and stablecoin issuers and owns currency, PSPs and KEPSS; CMA licenses exchanges, brokers, investment services, offerings and tokenisation. KRA owns tax; FRC and law-enforcement bodies retain AML and enforcement functions; courts and tribunals adjudicate. The National Treasury and CBK opened a separate draft National Payment System Policy and Bill on 21 September 2026; the policy anticipates implications for PSP licensing and remittance products that integrate tokenised or stablecoin arrangements, but it is a proposal, not current operating authority.
authority.boundary: Policy, proposed payment-law reform, category-specific licensing, AML registration, tax reporting, PSP authorization, settlement operation, investigation and adjudication are different capacities.

legal_objects.summary: The record separates Act-defined virtual assets and stablecoins, consumer assets, issuer reserve assets, custody and provider books, tax-reportable transactions, bank deposits, mobile-money balances, Kenya-shilling legal tender and KEPSS central-bank settlement. Central-bank digital fiat is excluded from the Act's virtual-asset definition.
legal_objects.boundary: A digital interface does not merge issuer liability, reserve backing, custody, bank or mobile-money claims, tax treatment, legal tender or final central-bank money.

permitted_activities.summary: Licensed categories cover wallets, exchanges and trading platforms, payment processing, brokerage, advice, management, offerings, tokenisation, token-issuance platforms and stablecoin issuance. Offering or admitting a stablecoin to trading also requires issuer status, CBK white-paper approval and publication; virtual-asset conversion to or from foreign currency requires separate CBK authorization.
permitted_activities.boundary: Possession, transitional operation, application, licence, category permission, white-paper approval, FX-conversion authorization and recurring production are separate states.

entry_gates.summary: Entry turns on the exact activity and regulator, complete application and due diligence, fit-and-proper and source-of-funds review, category capital and liquidity, local bank accounts, AML/CFT/CPF, cybersecurity, consumer and continuity controls, cross-border disclosure, tax duties and any separate FX authorization. The rules apply to foreign providers targeting Kenyan consumers or deriving Kenyan economic benefit.
entry_gates.boundary: Application, complete-file clock, grant, commencement within twelve months, capital compliance, exact service, transition status and current operation must be proved independently.

named_operating_actors.summary: CBK's 10 August 2026 PSP directory names Safaricom PLC, Airtel Money Kenya Limited and other legal persons for conventional payment services; Safaricom is authorized to issue, process, store, send and facilitate mobile-money payments. The November 2025 CBK/CMA notice said no VASP was then licensed. No post-regulations cutoff export joining a VASP legal person to category, conditions and commencement was located. For the bank overlay, CBK's 2025 supervision report defines an eight-bank Large peer group—KCB Bank Kenya, Equity Bank Kenya, Co-operative Bank of Kenya, Absa Bank Kenya, NCBA Bank Kenya, Stanbic Bank Kenya, I&M Bank and Diamond Trust Bank Kenya. Their own current materials prove different preparation states but no locally scoped bank-issued stablecoin, direct retail crypto dealing or production crypto-custody launch: KCB maps a possible future banking-partner role; Co-op has a risk/compliance assessment underway; Stanbic identifies possible partnership, payment-rail and custody implications; Absa Kenya is building virtual-asset custody capacity; NCBA and I&M publish market research; Equity and DTB disclose digital-banking transformation without a named crypto product.
named_operating_actors.boundary: A large-bank designation, PSP licence, strategy statement, compliance assessment, research note, capacity-building programme or parent-group capability is not a Kenyan VASP or stablecoin licence, product launch, reserve mandate, customer custody balance or recurring transaction.

claims_and_backing.summary: The final rules require a stablecoin holder claim against the issuer, issuance and redemption at par, two-working-day redemption, full reserve backing, permitted short-duration assets, legal segregation and insolvency remoteness, CBK-approved custody, at least 30% of received funds in segregated Kenyan trust accounts, quarterly stress tests and reserve audits. No named licensed issuer, coin, reserve pool, audit or redemption series was established.
claims_and_backing.boundary: A strong statutory architecture is not proof that a particular coin is licensed, backed, liquid, redeemable in practice, deposit-insured or sovereignly guaranteed.

domestic_rails.summary: KEPSS is CBK's production RTGS and its rules make accepted settlement final and irrevocable. Licensed mobile-money providers and other PSPs supply conventional retail payment records. The 21 September draft NPS reform seeks wider interoperability and expressly anticipates stablecoin- or token-integrated payment products, but it does not make a virtual-asset book final central-bank money. VASP books, custodial wallets, stablecoin ledgers and public blockchains remain separate records from KEPSS settlement.
domestic_rails.boundary: A draft interoperability policy, customer-visible speed, mobile-money value, bank credit, VASP execution, chain confirmation, stablecoin redemption and final central-bank settlement are not interchangeable.

cross_border_routes.summary: The regulations reach foreign providers that target Kenya, require cross-border-operation disclosure and impose a separate CBK authorization for virtual-asset/foreign-currency conversion. KCB's 25 September 2026 launch with TerraPay affiliate Mobex gives KCB Bank Kenya customers an operating incoming-diaspora-remittance endpoint, but the bank release identifies bank-account receipt and does not identify stablecoin funding, blockchain transfer, token redemption or on-chain settlement. Existing TLIP/TWIN/IOTA connectivity and ADAPT country implementation evidence concern trade documents and planned payment interoperability. None proves a recurring crypto payment corridor.
cross_border_routes.boundary: Legal reach, disclosure, conversion permission, a conventional remittance connection, trade credential, project-country list or planned interoperability is not payer funding, FX, token transfer, beneficiary receipt, final money, failure and correction; the map carries zero arcs.

operating_state.summary: The 2025 Act, final July 2026 regulations, tax rules, PSP regime, KEPSS and mobile money are operating legal or technical layers. Existing-provider transition remains open through 4 November 2026. The March 2026 VASP draft is superseded by the final gazette, while the September 2026 NPS policy and bill remain proposals. KCB's TerraPay/Mobex receipt service is an operating conventional remittance connection. Large-bank disclosures otherwise range from strategy and capacity-building to compliance review and market research; none supplies a Kenyan bank crypto launch receipt. CBDC remains monitoring and research rather than pilot or production.
operating_state.boundary: Enacted law, final rule, proposed payment reform, open transition, application, licence, bank preparation, conventional operating rail, crypto product launch, pilot, first transaction and recurring production are separate states.

scale.summary: CBK's July 2026 mobile-payments table reported 94.35 million registered accounts, 575,400 active agents, 221.07 million agent cash-in/cash-out transactions and KSh728.7 billion in agent cash-in/cash-out value. These contextualize the conventional digital-fiat ecosystem. No complete official VASP, private-stablecoin, crypto-customer, balance or transaction aggregate was established.
scale.boundary: Registered accounts are not unique or active users; agent cash activity is not total mobile-money flow, crypto adoption, stablecoin reserves, cross-border flow or central-bank settlement.

stress.summary: The 2025 Financial Sector Stability Report identified unlicensed digital trading apps and informal crypto-arbitrage ventures as a threat. A January 2025 DCI arrest report warned of crypto use outside formal systems to evade detection. Capital, reserves, audits, safeguards, freezing and seizure rules are prospective controls. No official national provider-failure or stablecoin-run series was located.
stress.boundary: A risk statement, arrest allegation, capital rule or intervention power is not an adjudicated loss, provider shortfall, recovered-asset amount or customer distribution.

correction_and_loss.summary: Correction may involve provider books, consumer attribution, bank or PSP records, blockchain state, CBK/CMA intervention, freezing or seizure, statutory management, liquidation and court disposition. Stablecoin reserves must be insolvency remote and a liquidating licensee must discharge consumer-fund liabilities as soon as practicable before ranking other creditors, while KEPSS finality fixes the accepted fiat entry.
correction_and_loss.boundary: Ledger correction, payment adjustment, regulatory intervention, asset freeze, seizure, statutory management, insolvency priority, recovery and restitution have separate clocks; none guarantees full recovery.

evidence_boundary.summary: The baseline uses enacted law, the final Government Printer instrument, official CBK/CMA notices and registers, Kenya Law, KRA, KEPSS and PSP records, CBK's bank-supervision report and institution-owned bank disclosures. It treats CBK's still-visible VASP-draft navigation as source-surface lag; treats the September NPS package as genuinely proposed; distinguishes local Kenyan-bank evidence from parent-group activity; labels mobile-money scale correctly; and preserves existing private-infrastructure owners only as bounded context.
evidence_boundary.boundary: Fresh research, a negative primary-source search or a foreign parent capability is not Chronicle promotion, investment advice, publication authority, a sourced route arc or permission to hand-edit the generated map.
